**Sources read (as excerpts only)**
- Enduring Word (David Guzik): https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/exodus-40/
- Precept Austin, which quotes Cassuto, Bush, Currid, Stuart and others: https://www.preceptaustin.org/exodus-40-commentary
- Matthew Henry: https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Exd/Exd_040.cfm

## 1. The traditional reading, verse by verse

**v. 1:** The work was finished, but Moses didn't set the tabernacle up until God told him to. Ellicott compares this with Moses waiting for God's call before going up Sinai in Exodus 24:16. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ebc/exodus-40.html
- Henry says the same: Moses waited for express orders, and it is good to have God going before us at every step. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Exd/Exd_040.cfm

**v. 2:** This date was about a year after Israel left Egypt. Guzik says it was a time to count God's great works and measure their own spiritual growth. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/exodus-40/
- JFB works out that building started within six months of the exodus and took another six months. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/jfb/Exd/Exd_040.cfm
- Ellicott thinks the work began in the sixth or seventh month and ended late in the year. New Year's Day was then the natural choice for opening the new structure. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ebc/exodus-40.html
- Henry's lesson is that it is good to start the year with some good work and put God first. He also says we must not put off a duty while waiting for a special day. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Exd/Exd_040.cfm
- Henry also notes that Israel didn't wait until they reached Canaan; they set it up in the wilderness. Being unsettled in life is no excuse for not serving God. (Same URL.)

**v. 3:** The tabernacle had to be put together according to God's pattern, just as it had been built to it. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/exodus-40/
- Ellicott: the ark, the most precious object, went in first and was then covered at once with the veil. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ebc/exodus-40.html

**v. 5:** "In front of the ark" means outside the veil, in the Holy Place, but closer to the veil than the table or lampstand (Ellicott). https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ebc/exodus-40.html

**vv. 9–11:** Pulpit's lesson: the anointing of everything with holy oil pictures the Spirit making holy and empowering all the means of grace God gives. https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/tpc/exodus-40.html

**v. 13:** Precept Austin, quoting Cassuto, says this verse applies only to the high priest. Anointing was the central rite of consecration, and only Aaron was anointed for the high priesthood. https://www.preceptaustin.org/exodus-40-commentary

**v. 15:**
- **How the sons were anointed.** Ellicott and JFB both point to Leviticus 8. There the oil was poured on Aaron's head, but his sons were only sprinkled with oil mixed with blood. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ebc/exodus-40.html ; https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/jfb/Exd/Exd_040.cfm
- Pulpit also calls the sons' anointing a lower form, which is why the high priest was sometimes called "the anointed priest." https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/tpc/exodus-40.html
- **"A permanent priesthood."** Bush, quoted on Precept Austin, says this first anointing counted for the whole line of ordinary priests, so later generations didn't need to be anointed again. https://www.preceptaustin.org/exodus-40-commentary

**v. 16:** Moses did everything God commanded. Henry adds that he did it in the order God set, "for God will be sought in the due order." https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Exd/Exd_040.cfm

**vv. 17–33 (the repeated phrase):**
- Henry counts "as the LORD commanded Moses" seven times in under fourteen verses. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Exd/Exd_040.cfm
- Currid, quoted on Precept Austin, also counts seven: vv. 19, 21, 23, 25, 27, 29, 32. https://www.preceptaustin.org/exodus-40-commentary
- Guzik counts it at least 19 times across chapters 36–40. He quotes G. Campbell Morgan: God's work must be done God's way, and people are always tempted to "improve" on God's plan. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/exodus-40/

**v. 20:** "The Testimony" means the two stone tablets Moses brought down from Sinai (Exodus 34:29). Ellicott adds that this verse doesn't prove the ark held nothing else. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ebc/exodus-40.html

**v. 23:** Henry: once the table was placed, the bread was set on it, "for God will never have his table unfurnished." https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Exd/Exd_040.cfm

**v. 25:** Ellicott says the lamps were lit at the proper time, in the evening (Exodus 30:8; Leviticus 24:3). https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ebc/exodus-40.html
- Henry says Moses lit them as soon as the lampstand was in place. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Exd/Exd_040.cfm

**vv. 26–29:** Henry: Moses started the service himself and then handed it to the appointed priests. God's gifts are meant to be used, not just displayed. He thinks Moses began the consecration at once, though it took seven days to complete. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Exd/Exd_040.cfm

**vv. 30–32:** The priests couldn't serve properly without ritual washing; God wanted service from clean hands and feet (Guzik). https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/exodus-40/
- Ellicott reads vv. 31–32 as an aside about how the basin was used later, not part of the first day. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ebc/exodus-40.html
- Stuart, quoted on Precept Austin, says these verses look ahead to the priests' ordination in Leviticus 8. https://www.preceptaustin.org/exodus-40-commentary

**v. 33:**
- **Fulfilment.** Precept Austin says this completes God's command in Exodus 25:8 to build a sanctuary so he could live among them. It also notes the usual "as the LORD commanded" phrase is missing here, because the work was now done. https://www.preceptaustin.org/exodus-40-commentary
- **A model of heaven.** Guzik says the finished tabernacle was an earthly copy of a heavenly reality. That is why parts of it show up in the Bible's pictures of heaven (Revelation 4, Isaiah 6). https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/exodus-40/
- **The opening day.** JFB believes the people were probably gathered around the tabernacle for the dedication, though the text doesn't say so. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/jfb/Exd/Exd_040.cfm

**v. 34:**
- **Obedience welcomed the glory.** Guzik says Israel didn't earn the glory by obeying, but their obedience welcomed it. He adds that God doesn't love us more when we obey, yet walking in his truth brings blessing. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/exodus-40/
- **God takes up residence.** Henry compares this to creation: God made the earth and then put man in it. Here Moses finished the tabernacle and God moved in. Henry sees the Shekinah (God's visible presence) as a preview of the Word becoming flesh. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Exd/Exd_040.cfm
- **The cloud's meaning (JFB).** The cloud gave shade from the heat and was a sign of God's presence. It was also a picture of the Mosaic age, which left much hidden compared with the gospel. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/jfb/Exd/Exd_040.cfm
- **Restored favour.** A writer quoted on Precept Austin sees this as proof that God had restored his favour after the golden calf. He also sees it as a pledge of Christ, the true Shekinah, living among us in human flesh. https://www.preceptaustin.org/exodus-40-commentary

**v. 35:**
- **The same as Solomon's temple.** The same thing happened when Solomon's temple was dedicated (1 Kings 8:10–11; 2 Chronicles 5:14). https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/exodus-40/ ; https://www.preceptaustin.org/exodus-40-commentary
- **What stopped Moses.** Pulpit infers that Moses tried to enter. It says the glory inside stopped him, not the cloud outside. https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/tpc/exodus-40.html
- **Christ enters where Moses could not.** JFB and Henry both say the verse shows human weakness before God's unveiled glory. Christ, our forerunner, has entered for us and invites us to come boldly to the mercy seat. JFB calls Christ "the true tabernacle." https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/jfb/Exd/Exd_040.cfm ; https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Exd/Exd_040.cfm

**vv. 36–37:**
- **Moses' prayer answered.** Guzik: this answers Moses' prayer in Exodus 33:14. God stayed with Israel despite the golden calf. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/exodus-40/
- **Guidance tied to the tabernacle.** A writer quoted on Precept Austin says God's guidance was tied to the tabernacle; Israel's movements depended on what the cloud over it did. https://www.preceptaustin.org/exodus-40-commentary
- **Desert torches.** JFB cites Faber: desert travellers, and the armies of Darius and Alexander, were led by torches that gave smoke by day and fire by night. JFB says this custom shows why the miracle was needed and fitting. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/jfb/Exd/Exd_040.cfm

**v. 38:**
- **God's presence made fact.** Guzik quotes Cole: Exodus ends with the promise of 29:45 fulfilled. God's presence moves from theology to fact. Guzik adds that the book ends in hope despite Israel's weakness. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/exodus-40/
- **Only over the tabernacle now.** JFB: the cloud used to appear in different places but now rested only on the tabernacle. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/jfb/Exd/Exd_040.cfm
- **For all 40 years.** Precept Austin: God's presence stayed with Israel the whole 40 years. https://www.preceptaustin.org/exodus-40-commentary

---

## 2. Where Protestant traditions differ

I didn't find any. I couldn't reach the Reformed, Baptist, Wesleyan, Pentecostal or Lutheran sites, so I can't say whether they read this chapter differently.

One view leans toward the Spirit's work. A writer quoted on Precept Austin (probably G. Campbell Morgan, but the excerpt doesn't name him) links the glory filling the tabernacle (v. 34) to the Spirit coming at Pentecost and living in each believer. Precept Austin also says the cloud that filled the tabernacle then guided Israel (v. 36), just as the Spirit who fills believers also leads them (Matthew 3:16; 4:1). https://www.preceptaustin.org/exodus-40-commentary

---

## 3. Other views

- **v. 15, Jewish (rabbinic) reading.** Ellicott and Pulpit both report it: the first anointing of Aaron's sons was never repeated, and later ordinary priests took office without being anointed. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ebc/exodus-40.html ; https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/tpc/exodus-40.html
- **Modern scholarship, Catholic and Orthodox views, and debated modern teaching:** I didn't find anything. I couldn't reach netbible.org, bibleodyssey.org, newadvent.org, catholic.com or oca.org.
